subject: math

objective.text: Solve multi-step word problems with tape diagrams. Check answers by rounding.

explanations.title: Multi-step problems
explanations.text: Find each missing amount one step at a time. Then add or subtract to find what the question asks.

explanations.title: More than one way
explanations.text: You can find each amount and add. Or you can add like units first. Both ways are right.

explanations.title: Check with the diagram
explanations.text: Look at the tape diagram. Round each amount and add the rounded amounts. Your exact answer should be close.

explanations.title: Count in thousands
explanations.text: 2 thousand more and 2 thousand fewer cancel out. Those two weeks add up to 2 times week 1.

examples.title: Fabrics at a factory
examples.text: Cotton 11,650 meters. Silk 11,650 minus 4,950 is 6,700 meters. Wool 6,700 minus 3,500 is 3,200 meters. The total is 21,550 meters.

examples.title: Ice cream cones
examples.text: Chocolate 12,789. Cookie dough 9,324. Peanut butter 10,402. Vanilla 13,788. The total is 46,303 cones.

examples.title: Omelets in June
examples.text: Week 1 10,345. Week 2 9,249. Week 3 12,345. Week 4 8,345. The total is 40,284 omelets.

questions.text: 30,436 people went skiing in January and February. 16,009 went in February. How many people went skiing in January?
16,009 people went skiing in February and 14,427 in January. How many fewer people went in January than in February?
A factory used 11,650 meters of cotton. It used 4,950 fewer meters of silk than cotton. How many meters of silk did it use?
The factory used 6,700 meters of silk. It used 3,500 fewer meters of wool than silk. How many meters of wool did it use?
The factory used 11,650 meters of cotton, 6,700 of silk and 3,200 of wool. How many meters were used in all?
In the fabric problem, is the part or the total unknown?

questions.text: A shop sold 9,324 cookie dough cones. It sold 1,078 more peanut butter cones than cookie dough cones. How many peanut butter cones did it sell?
The shop sold 12,789 chocolate cones. It sold 999 more vanilla cones than chocolate cones. How many vanilla cones did it sell?
The shop sold 12,789 chocolate, 9,324 cookie dough, 10,402 peanut butter and 13,788 vanilla cones. How many cones did it sell in all?
Round the four flavors to the nearest thousand and add: 12,789, 9,324, 10,402 and 13,788. What is the estimate?

questions.text: A restaurant sold 10,345 omelets in week 1. In week 2 it sold 1,096 fewer. How many omelets did it sell in week 2?
Week 1 had 10,345 omelets. Week 3 had 2 thousand more. How many omelets were sold in week 3?
Week 1 had 10,345 omelets. Week 4 had 2 thousand fewer. How many omelets were sold in week 4?
The four weeks had 10,345, 9,249, 12,345 and 8,345 omelets. How many omelets were sold in June?
Round the four weeks to the nearest thousand and add: 10,345, 9,249, 12,345 and 8,345. What is the estimate?

questions.text: Park A covers 4,926 square kilometers. It is 1,845 square kilometers larger than Park B. How large is Park B?
Park C is 4,006 square kilometers larger than Park A, which is 4,926. How large is Park C?
Park A is 4,926, Park B is 3,081 and Park C is 8,932 square kilometers. What is the area of all three parks?
Round the three parks to the nearest thousand and add: 4,926, 3,081 and 8,932. What is the estimate?
The estimate is 17,000 and the exact answer is 16,939. Is the answer reasonable?
At a fair there were 49,563 men. There were 2,872 more women than men. How many women were there?
At the fair there were 22,869 children, 49,563 men and 52,435 women. How many people were at the fair?
Number A is 4,676. Number B is 10,043 greater than A. What is B?
Number B is 14,719. Number C is 2,610 less than B. What is C?
A is 4,676, B is 14,719 and C is 12,109. What is the total value of A, B and C?
A store sold 11,795 baseballs. It sold 4,150 fewer basketballs than baseballs. How many basketballs did it sell?
A store sold 21,650 balls in all, 11,795 baseballs and 7,645 basketballs. The rest were footballs. How many footballs did it sell?

hints.text: Find the digit that changes. See how it changes each time.
Think how many grams make one kilogram.
Find the missing amount first. Then compare or add.
Find one amount at a time. Use the last amount you found for the next one.
Add all the amounts together to find the total.
Round each amount to the nearest thousand. Then add or subtract.
Compare the exact answer with your estimate. Are they close?
Subtract the amounts you know from the total to find the rest.

assets_required.why_this_method: The lesson uses tape diagrams drawn by the child. The child cannot draw them here.
assets_required.description: A multi-bar tape diagram with an estimate box. The child sets the amounts for each bar, sees the total, and compares an estimate with the exact answer.
must_show_exactly: Up to four tapes with labeled amounts
An estimate box with a choice of place to round to
A compare row for the estimate and exact answer
assets_required.interaction: Child sets the amounts for each tape. The widget shows the total, then the child enters an estimate and sees if it is close.
assets_required.alt_text: A tape diagram with several bars, a total bracket and an estimate box.
assets_required.generation_caption: A clean tape diagram with up to four labeled bars, a total bracket with a variable and an estimate box. [Build by code]
assets_required.review_notes: Source tape diagrams are drawn by the child. Build from the printed numbers.
